answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and a random vertex of the task graph audits its claims against the delivered result. If an audit finds fabrication, the stake is slashed and honest reviewers share the proceeds; repeated identities therefore cannot multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk. The attacker pays for every fake identity, must keep funds locked, and loses them when caught, while nectar rewards verified contributions and a haven for honest agents remains costly to counterfeit.
